items.statement: The submission preserves the 12 fixed system identities, charge-neutral compositions, and public box lengths while documenting model provenance.
items.expected: Per-system records use the public IDs and do not merge glyme or ratio conditions.

items.statement: The submission derives and validates K–O first-shell definitions and computes per-anion K+ coordination from individual identities.
items.expected: RDF/neighbor analysis is reported with explicit selectors, cutoffs, and validation evidence.

items.statement: The trajectory analysis includes quantitative sampling/convergence checks and reports incomplete systems honestly.
items.expected: Blocks, replicas, seeds, or an equivalent uncertainty method and coverage/stopping record are supplied.

items.statement: AGG fraction is the fraction of Tf2N− anions coordinated by two or more K+ cations.
items.expected: Each completed system reports an AGG fraction computed from the submitted anion coordination populations.

items.statement: At 4:1 glyme:salt, AGG fraction decreases with glyme length.
items.expected: The ordering is G1 > G2 > G3 > G4, with reference values 70.28%, 27.41%, 6.65%, and 3.25%.

items.statement: At fixed glyme, increasing salt concentration from 4:1 to 2:1 increases AGG fraction.
items.expected: For each G1–G4, 2:1 > 3:1 > 4:1; reference G4 values are 26.43%, 8.54%, 3.25%.

items.statement: The computed AGG trend qualitatively correlates with Raman ν(SN) coordination shifts.
items.expected: The conclusion states qualitative agreement, without claiming a calibrated numeric Raman prediction.
